summary: The revised performance EC now pins concrete workloads, thresholds, fail-closed prerequisites, and independent ratio calculations, so assertion specificity is repaired. It is still not semantically sufficient because the referenced test executables contradict those assertions: Kafka still skips successfully and all three performance gates still delegate pass/fail to Tape's implementation helpers. The generated-client, competitor-feature oracle, and two security evidence blockers are unchanged. The generated inventory also remains structurally stale at 15 of 28 source cases.
findings: tape-competitor-performance-kafka-replay-win / topic-replay-kafka-local-backlog-win: the revised EC now requires the production gate to fail closed, but `tests/tape_vs_kafka.rs` still returns success when Docker/Kafka is unavailable or fixed port 9092 is occupied (`spawn_kafka_broker` returns `None` and the test returns). Make the referenced runner fail on every missing prerequisite, or point this required case at a different mandatory runner that cannot report success without completing the pinned Kafka workload and 1.5x assertion.

tape-competitor-performance-local-regression-and-calibration-ledger plus the NATS/Kafka win cases / topic-replay-competitor-performance-baseline: the revised EC correctly pins fixed thresholds and says the tests do not trust Tape's verdict helpers, but the referenced executables still call `tape::bench::verify_report` and `tape::bench::verify_external_replay_win`; the NATS/Kafka reports and `win_claim` are also constructed by `tape::bench::external_replay_win`. Make the external test layer independently compare the observed fields against the EC's 5,000/50,000/5,000-us budgets and independently compute/assert each >=1.5 ratio, without using implementation-owned verdict or win-claim functions.

tape-cli-interface-generated-clients / tape-openapi-generated-client-contract: the EC command remains `cargo test -p tape --test backup -- --nocapture`, but `tests/backup.rs` is entirely gated by `#![cfg(feature = "backup")]` and tests backup transport rather than `tape spec gen`; the command can execute zero tests and never prove TypeScript, Python, or Rust client generation. Revise this case to invoke a non-zero dedicated generated-client test (for example the existing `spec_gen_verbs_parse_and_generate` binary test or a stronger end-to-end equivalent) and assert the emitted artifacts and Tape route scope directly.

tape-competitor-feature-parity-topic-exchange-functional / topic-replay-competitor-feature-matrix: `tests/competitor_feature_parity.rs` still defines every competitor capability as hard-coded booleans in `matrix()` and then asserts those same booleans, so no independent competitor oracle can falsify the Kafka/Redpanda/Pulsar/JetStream/RabbitMQ claims. Revise the case to consume a versioned externally sourced baseline or real peer conformance evidence, with provenance pinned outside the implementation and test assertions that compare Tape behavior against that independent oracle.

tape-security-hardening-access-control / tape-topic-subscription-authz-boundary: its command still runs only `service_auth` and `service_admission`, but the final assertion additionally claims redacted authorization audit fields and a payload-free successful admin-backup audit event. Revise the case to execute an audit-capture journey that performs credential rotation and an authenticated admin backup and asserts the emitted redacted event, or split/remove claims not exercised by this command.

tape-security-hardening-guard-scan / guard-static-runtime-evidence: the EC still claims guard attaches meter evidence for bearer-auth request-boundary cases, but `vat.toml` runs meter over `--test cli_contract`, whose cases do not exercise required bearer authentication or topic RBAC. Revise the tool case/runner to meter the real `service_auth` security journey (and retain non-zero-test enforcement), or narrow the assertion so it does not claim auth evidence.
